title: Day 2 of my trial and I’m NOT subscribing when it ends
body:
I really wanted to like Structured because it advertises itself as being especially helpful for people with ADHD. Unfortunately, my experience during the trial was the opposite.

The AI was the main reason I considered paying for the app, but it ended up creating more work instead of saving me time. I would ask it to schedule tasks, then have to go back and manually fix the schedule. When I asked it to move a multi-step outing (such as a library trip with walking there, signing up for library cards, browsing, and walking home), it only moved one task and left the others behind. That completely broke the plan and forced me to reorganize everything myself.

Recurring tasks were another major frustration. When I tried to delete a recurring task, I wasn’t given the expected options to delete just one occurrence, all future occurrences, or the entire series. Instead, I had to edit the recurrence before I could finally remove it. That’s confusing and unnecessarily time-consuming.

Importing Apple Reminders was another disappointing experience. I have well-organized reminder lists with headings, tasks, and subtasks. Structured completely flattened everything during the import, splitting headings, tasks, and subtasks into individual inbox items. Instead of preserving the organization, it created a cluttered mess.

To make matters worse, there was no way to select those imported items as a group and hide or remove them. I had to tap each one individually. The only workaround I found was going into the app’s settings and manually disabling each Reminders list one by one. Even then, one of the lists continued appearing in my inbox after it had been turned off. I had to repeatedly enable and disable the list before Structured finally removed those items.

The app also advertises swipe gestures to quickly delete, postpone, or manage tasks, but those gestures didn’t work for me at all.

After spending my trial fighting with the AI, fixing broken schedules, cleaning up imported reminders, and manually reorganizing tasks, I realized I could accomplish the same thing by using Apple Calendar alongside Reminders. The AI was supposed to be the feature that justified the subscription, but in my experience it wasn’t reliable enough to do that.

The concept behind Structured is excellent, and I can see why people are excited about it. However, the current AI and task management experience simply wasn’t dependable enough for me to trust with my daily planning. Instead of reducing my mental load, it increased it.

title: Brilliant Use of AI
body: I have a lot of issues with staying on taks, or splitting up my day to tackle several large tasks. I tend to just throw myself into a single thing and lose sight that multiple projects and things need to get done, and I end up poorly managing my time. This app really helps with that. Now, I spent five minutes in the morning planning out my day in my journal, making a list, jotting down my durations, and then I hope into structure and use the AI assistant. I feed it the list and then give it parameters like durations, gaps, lunch breaks, and specify where subtasks should go. It all takes less than five minutes, and the app builds out my day and plans it to the minute. What’s even better is if something comes up during the day, I can hope into the AI assistant and get it to rebuild my day making adjustments for completed tasks, etc. It’s really been a game changer for me. And I don’t need to use it every day, just the days where  I really need to be on point and focused. And I love that I can build it all out on my laptop, and then have my phone remind me as I’m running around working of when I should be switching focuses, or even taking breaks. Worth every cent.

title: Useful. However Causes Excess Battery Drain
body: Honestly, this is a really good application. I really love the UI and it’s pretty easy to use. I especially love how there is a Web version which allows me to use it for my day to day planning at work. Overall it’s intuitive and very good for people who like to stay organized and use daily planners. The one caveat with this application and the only reason I didn’t give it 5 stars (and also the reason I am on the fence about subscribing for it) is the battery drain on this app. It appears that this application has NOT been optimized AT ALL for battery efficiency. I am on the iPhone 17 Pro Max, my battery is fantastic. That said - THIS APP DRAINS IT. After several days of usage, I’ve been able to determine it drains about 0.36% of battery per minute. Which I mean, doesn’t seem like much at first glance. But when you run the math on it, that means just using this app for about 25ish minutes a day will drain 10% of your battery.. That’s a lot for a todo/daily planner application. The first day I got the app and I set up my schedule and all my repeating tasks, I used the app for about 1 hour and 5 minutes of screen on time, that resulted in 25% battery usage. To be blunt, that’s horrendously poor optimization. Just for perspective, highly resource intensive applications such as BlackMagic Camera when filming in 60 FPS at 4K use the EXACT SAME amount of battery as this application per minute. There is no reason a daily planner should drain just as much and sometimes more than a highly intensive and resource demanding video recording application. This should definitely be investigated.

title: Good App: Why 4 Stars?
body:
Hi, I’m from Canada. I hardly write any reviews but it kept asking me for one.. so here I am. I’m gonna keep it short, here are 3 main reasons why I like using this app as someone who’s been using it for about 4 years now. 

1. Organization
2. Discipline 
3. Structured App + Notion App = best combo
————————————
1. It helps me stay organized for my daily tasks and simple tasks that I plan to do. 

2. It does help me to stay disciplined for the gym, my walks and my runs. I use it more as a fitness schedule, but you can use it for pretty much everything. 

3. As a first-year college student, using this app for my fitness schedule and the Notion app for my school schedule and as an assignment tracker is one of the best combos.

(Also, sometimes I do get frustrated when certain apps that I would like to use are hard to use, so it’s good because this app is very easy to use.)
————————————
Why 4 stars? 
-The prices of the in-app purchases are too high for students. We don’t have money like that. Not everyone can afford to pay for it. So, I would like to suggest if you guys could do student prices, it would help some of us.

Bye.

title: Great but...
body:
I never write reviews but I felt the need to for this app. It's great, I love it. If a reader is debating whether or not to give it a try, you should, design, interface, intuitiveness, features, etc, it's solid.

That being said, there are a few features that would really put it over the top and for me, would justify the annual subscription.
1) I sometimes like to move tasks around the day by dragging them - which the app does perfectly. However it's really difficult to drop it precisely where i want (example at the start time I want) because of the collapsible nature of the schedule. Ideally the day's layout would expand fully when modifying the schedule
2) Would be great if i could drag multiple tasks at the same time, say I'm running late and want to push everything back by 30min, currently it seems the only way to do this is one by one which is a bit tedious
3) Would also be great if i could drag the upper/lower edge of the task bubble on the planner view to make it start earlier or finish later without moving the bubble entirely. Currently i would have to open the task and edit it. not a big deal but something i'd appreciate

on a side note, the macOS version doesn't seem to be showing the task i just created from the macOS version itself, even though it syncs and is visible on my ios version. Admittedly, i'm on macOS 14.4 so maybe i just need to update to the latest version to fix this.

Hope the feedback might be useful to the devs! Otherwise, love the app, keep it up!

title: Lacks Most Basic Functionalities
body:
I needed calendar integration, so I upgraded to a yearly subscription.  I utterly regretted 2 mins after starting using the app.  It lacks the most basic day-to-day functionalities one would expect from any task management app.  For starters, there is no search function whatsoever!  I couldn’t believe that until I got the confirmation from the help section of the developer’s own website.  NO SEARCH AND NO LIST VIEW.  This means you’d better REMEMBER every task you ever created.  God forbids, if you ever want to look up a specific task, you’ll actually need to flip through every day, one day at a time.  That ALONE would render the app completely useless.  But it gets worse.  There’s no “back to today” either.  You’ll literally have to pull up the calendar and find today’s date to click on.   And the whole flow to create a task is awkward too.  I created a few tasks without realizing the wrong date was selected.  Then afterwards, of course I couldn’t find them.  Remember, NO SEARCH and NO LIST VIEW!  I flipped through weeks worth of daily tasks to locate them.

I’m genuinely shocked at the overwhelmingly positive reviews for such an instantly laughably useless app.  I would say daily view, which is the only view, does look pleasing to the eyes.  I guess a lot of people have tons of time looking at a pretty planner and nothing important to do, because if they do have any real tasks, the planner isn’t going to help them accomplish them.

title: Please slow more allow one notification sound! Would be soo much more useful!
body:
I have adhd, but also ASD and OCD, but because of a neurological injury, I have short term memory loss and it looks like severe ADHD. It’s driving me insane. This app would be perfect, exactly what I need, if only I could do more than one sound. Unfortunately, even on the most annoying one, my brain has tuned it out when I’m overwhelmed and my SPD is in overload, and I don’t hear it anymore. The problem is it just neighs all day unless I make there are way less tasks, but then it’s no longer of use because I won’t remember what I need to do. 

It’s either select complete on them all, even if I haven’t done them, just to make the noise stop, or my brain will just turn off anyway and ignore it subconsciously. The biggest issue is that I never know what each neigh is for without picking up my phone and then… I’ve picked up my phone. And I start trying to accomplish things on there, but instantly forget what I was doing and end up going in loops and getting distracted, trying to remember what I was doing, and ultimately  completing basically nothing. Yes, I see the notifications then, but it doesn’t pull me away from the doomsday scroll or starting 500 things on my phone I needed to do, but never finish. I have issues with hyperfocus not just because of adhd but because of the autism and ocd as well, so I do not want to touch my phone. Yes, I know there’s a blocking feature, but I have many reasons why I need that to not be there. Kids being the big one. Didn't work for me.

Anyway, long story short- please add the ability to use more than one sound just like the colours!!  Auditory prompts are so helpful! But as primarily visual currently, I am still just relying on Alexa which is.. a  nightmare, lol. She never stops when asked or gets things right, and my kids try to turn off before I can’t even hear or rememebr what I was even supposed to do anyway. Today has been a perfect example of this, so here I am at this app again and wishing so much that this feature existed because I’m discouraged. 

An app like this is a life saver- it just needs a few tweaks! 🙏🏻 Otherwise it’s great!

Thanks STRUCTURED!

title: Nice App, but room to improve it
body:
I like this application, Ive been using it for roughly 48 hours now and its a clean user-friendly planner. However there is some room to improve here on this application to take this to a 5-star...

1. the mobile app shows bubbles under each of the days where events occur... I have 5 reoccuring events each day causing this top bar to be an absolute UI mess with zero purpose for me now. I would really like a way to toggle this feature on/off in the settings. For people like me that have so many events each day, I want the bubbles to disappear from my calendar-week Ui bar, that way there is nothing there to distract me.

2. Although this app is available on Mac, I can say it is really not optimized properly for it. It takes several clicks on any part of the Ui for the app to recognize a user input request. Ive had instances where Ive had to mash the mouse click on the add button for the app to recognize that I want to create a new event.

3. The introduction needs to be redesigned. Im not super pleased that the system introduces you to its features by adding a bunch of random tasks to your planner -- forcing the end user to have to manually delete each event first before getting the opportunity to start building their planner. its unavoidable, its a UX nightmare, and it frustrates me. Please just switch this to a simple walk-through and give users a blank slate.

4. You have a good opportunity here to also build in some feature that supports habit tracking and displaying that to end users... I want to see how many times this week I completed my "Daily Workout" task in my planner. I want to see how many times I missed checking off the "Cook Dinner" task! At the end of the month this will help me visualize my habits and tailor my next-months planner to it.

Overall, this app is a wonderful app with some areas of improvement. I truly believe that if you consider my feedback and that of your other users then you are on the fast-track to making this one of the top applications on App Store.

Also, in the same idea, a checkbox that makes a task more "for informational purposes", a bit like a note or comment, which still allows you to place other tasks in this place.

Traduction: Ça serait très intéressant si nous pouvions cocher une case qui permettrait de prioriser une tâche, comme un rendez-vous important. Si cette case est cochée la tâche pourrait sonner comme une alarme sur le cellulaire et aussi être rajoutée dans la section calendrier pour donner un aperçu plus global des rendez-vous important.  Aussi, dans la même idée, une case à cocher qui rend une tâche plus « a titre informative », un peu comme une note ou un commentaire, qui permet quand même de placer d’autres tâches à cet endroit.

Overall, really great app that I would recommend to those who have a hard time prioritizing or getting through their tasks!

title: Great for visual planning helpful with ADHD and executive functions
body:
This has helped with my ADHD and issues with executive functions. I've been working on implementing this with my wife and kids as well as my own routines and work projects. Having this across all devices, very reasonable price point, and the focus mode on current tasks are fantastic. This has been a game changer. 

I do have some notes on improving things on the desktop, and perhaps mobile too? It does get a bit busy when adding multiples things and calendars. As I mentioned I'm using this to also plan with my family schedule so things often overlap. 

MAKE THE CURRENT TIME MORE EVIDENT. Perhaps a subtle background block or gradient progressing the entirety of the app background as the daily time progresses, or a simple line through main area mivng with the current time, maybe a solid container around the current time as well using the chosen app colour? 

OVERAPPING ITEMS. I think it would be helpful to make the overlap more evident. Perhaps indicate how much time the overlap is "Tasks are overlapping by 15 mins" and have the times it's overlapping on the left for example. Could you look at indenting the overlapping tasks, or having them display side by side, or collapsable as a group? Maybe an option to toggle specific calendars more easily? 

CHECKLIST INDICATION. The icon is a bit misleading being a solid grey box with a checkmark even though it shows the tally of items check via text beside it. THis makes me think those items are checked off, just a visual thing for me. Perhaps a drop down arrow in the box instead? Or using the outline version of the checkbox icon instead of solid?

Just suggestions from someone with ADHD and being very visual. Seeing time displayed this way is great. More visual the better!

title: Efficient and efficient
body:
I was looking for an app to help keep track of my To Do lists and to help actually get them completed. 

This app has filled that need! It syncs w my calendars but also offers up free time periods during which other items can be scheduled. 

There is also a general To-Do list where I can quickly add something and select when I’ll have time to complete it at a later date. If I find I have a gap in my day, I simply refer to this list and add it in to my schedule. 

You can colour code and add icons so for example, I have different colours for work, family, social and self care items or schedules. 

In a short time I have completed things I’ve been meaning to do for months. I’m now going to add a schedule for household maintenance and projects. 

Only suggestion so far would be to have the ability to drag your items to different time slots so if you’re running late you can rearrange your schedule. And a type search for the icons to find the one you want more quickly.

title: 2 Major Issues
body:
In general, this app is pretty good, but there are two major issues I’ve encountered that ruin it. 

1. While the option to copy tasks from a previous day is great, I hate that I put in my schedule for the week, then have to scan through the next month to delete all of the tasks that were randomly repeated. There’s no rhyme or reason to it, it’s just wasting time. 

2. The widget is so frustratingly useless. I have never seen a widget that is so non-functional. You can’t cross off tasks without it opening the app and you can’t scroll through the tasks for the day. It’s basically just a screenshot of the list. My biggest complaint, though, is that it never updates itself. As I’m typing this, the widget hasn’t updating my tasks since 1pm yesterday. In order to have it show the tasks for today, I will have to delete the widget, re-add it to my homepage (it will probably be blank when I do that), then hard restart my phone, maybe a couple times. It’s ridiculous that I have to do this almost every single day. The app is fully updated, so there’s no reason for this.

title: THE DAY PLANNER OF MY DREAMS
body:
Firstly, this app is incredible. Highly recommend it.

I wasn't sure I'd ever be able to find an app like this that did everything I needed, while also being simple to use - and aesthetically pleasing... while not costing a fortune...
Then I came across this app in the AppStore and downloaded it on a whim. I am in love with the user interface. It looks exactly how I imagined my "perfect day planner" to look.... I thought it might be missing features that I wanted, but this developer is a genius (!!!) and thought of everything. I'm genuinely excited to see what comes out in the future updates. I don't even write reviews very often - I just really love how this app performs and couldn't imagine a better day planner for my phone. I really appreciate all of the thought and functionality that went into the app. I even JUMPED at the chance to opt into the premium version, which is something i never thought I would say about an app! Truly the day planner of my dreams - thank you!! :)
